question: Who has taken over as the 26th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramesh Sivamani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Paramesh Sivamani took over as the 26th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard in 2023.
 
• He has had a distinguished career in the Indian Coast Guard, holding various key positions.
 
• Before becoming the Director General, he served as the Additional Director General of the Coast Guard.
 
• He has been instrumental in enhancing the operational capabilities and modernizing the fleet of the Indian Coast Guard.
 
• His leadership is expected to further strengthen the maritime security and search and rescue operations along India's coastline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Coast Guard**

 
 
• The Indian Coast Guard was formally established on 18 August 1978 by the Coast Guard Act, 1978, of the Parliament of India.
 
• Its primary role includes search and rescue operations, maritime law enforcement, and environmental protection.
 
• The Indian Coast Guard operates under the Ministry of Defence.
 
• The organization operates a wide range of vessels, aircraft, and helicopters to perform its duties effectively.
 
 
 
• **Director General of the Indian Coast Guard**
 
 
• The Director General is the chief of the Indian Coast Guard.
 
• This position is equivalent to a three-star rank in the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The Director General is responsible for the overall command and administration of the Coast Guard.
 
• The role includes strategic planning, operational readiness, and coordination with other maritime agencies.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Security**
 
 
• Maritime security involves protecting the nation’s maritime interests against threats such as piracy, terrorism, and smuggling.
 
• The Indian Coast Guard plays a crucial role in ensuring maritime security through regular patrols and surveillance.
 
• It collaborates with the Indian Navy, Marine Police, and other international maritime agencies.
 
• Effective maritime security is essential for safeguarding trade routes and national security.
